lastCompletedStory.title: Add cam issue list --json machine mode

nextStoryContext: US-002 added `cam issue list --json` (index.ts parseIssueArgs 'list' branch gains a `--json` flag, combinable with `--all`; ParsedIssueArgs 'list' member now carries `json: boolean`). The pure derivation lives in src/issues/list.ts as deriveBacklogJson(backlog, { includeShipped }) -> { counts, plannable, byStage }, reusing the now-exported compareBacklogEntries comparator (ranked-first/ascending-rank/numeric-id) for BOTH plannable and byStage ordering -- this is deliberately NOT selectPlannableIssue's WSJF-aware champion pick (CAM-203), which answers a different question (single winner vs. total-order list). plannable membership is isPlannable (src/issues/plannable.ts via select.ts's re-export), evaluated against the FULL backlog array (every stage), never a status:'open'-pre-filtered subset, because isBlocked needs to see blockers in any stage. Row shape is { id, title, rank } with rank normalized to `null` (never omitted) for unranked entries, since JSON.stringify silently drops undefined-valued keys and the AC's oracle expects the key to always be present. src/commands/issue-list.ts's runIssueList gained a `json?: boolean` option: when true and issue_system is 'none', it writes deriveBacklogJson's JSON.stringify output directly via process.stdout.write with ZERO emitTitle/heading decoration (pure JSON.parse-able stdout); 'linear'/'github' backends ignore --json entirely and keep printing their existing hint (the JSON contract is 'none'-only). US-003 (spine guard banning inline === 'specified' outside plannable.ts) can now encode the grep `grep -rElE "===\s*['\"]specified['\"]" src --include='*.ts' | grep -v '^src/vendor/'` as a test -- it still returns only src/issues/plannable.ts after this story (verified). US-004 (docs: mandate backlog derivation via `cam issue list --json` only) can now point at this exact JSON shape as the canonical machine contract.
